text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Daniel arap Moi announces a general amnesty for any subversive elements if they own up within three weeks.
- Criminal Investigation Department and Anti-Narcotic Unit officers arrest a coffee estate manager over the growing of opium poppy used as raw material for heroin.
- Kenya's ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) party secretary-general Joseph Kamotho says minority tribes countrywide will be marginalised if the constitution is changed.
- The Child Welfare Society of Kenya says the number of street children in Kenya's major towns is on the increase.
- The Kenyan government launches sale of an additional 11.9 million of its shares in Kenya Commercial Bank at an offer price of 50 shillings per share.
- Giant milk plant Kenya Cooperative Creameries chairman Stanley Metto loses a bid to restrain the Kenya Times from publishing allegedly defamatory and libellous articles against him.
- President Moi and Mozambican President Joaquim Chissano call for strengthening of bilateral ties between their countries through joint Permanent Commission.

- Cabinet Minister Kipkalya Kones refutes claims by some leaders from Bomet and Kericho districts, in Moi's native Rift Valley province, that he is planning to buy the Sotik Kenya Cooperative Creameries milk plant.

- The government has lost more than 200 million shillings in unpaid duty from the Turkwell Gorge Hydro-Electrical Project. It alleges company associated with project irregularly cleared goods using forged duty exemption letters claiming the goods were for Turkwell.
